title: Side pad v1.1 / Round 5: placement and padding ranges vs children aged 2–5
frame: Chair world mm, z up, seat surface z 20, child centreline x 0, left pad at +x. Front view, looking at the child.

chair.note: Simplified from the viewer meshes (geodata.json bounding boxes): armrest inner face x ~134, wing inner line x ~134. Mesh slices (raw/ps1_J_D, ps1_RiBH): in the pad band y −27…55 the armrest is x ≥ 135 and only up to z 149.4; its z 197.8 top is the rear block (y ≥ 62), and the wing starts at y 65.5. So the depth piece never meets the armrest at any height; the limit on width is the joint stack (arm end x 128.1 − tenon 13 − margin − pad-screw head − floor 6 ⇒ pad back ≤ ~106).

pad.contact_formula: x_contact = pad back x − 4.5 shell − foam − 2 cover (at the pad apex, y 34, where the chest is widest; the front edge wraps 7.5 mm further in)
pad.foam_note: One depth piece (D0); the child's width is set by the foam. Foam from the listed stock only: 5 = one 5 mm Super2 EVA sheet, 10 = one 10 mm sheet, 20 (standard) = 2 × 10 EVA laminated or 5 EVA + 15 HD top, 30 = 5 EVA + 25 HD top (padding_research build-up B). Cover 3 mm SBR neoprene (listed 4000031372319). Use: 2y P5 30 (or 20), 2y P50 20, ~3–4 y 10, 5y P50 10, 5y P95 5 (firm, thin: the price of not moving the arm end).
pad.reference_cushion_check: Viewer mesh D0: cushion min x 65.5, face at apex ≈ 69.5 (30 mm incl. cover, old FS reference); formula now gives 66.5 for 30 mm foam + 3 mm cover.

gap_rule_note: Manufacturers specify a "snug" fit, not a number (Spex). Working rule used here: −5…+10 mm per side = OK (light contact, room to breathe and for a T-shirt); +10…+20 = loose (child can lean before support); > +20 = no support; −5…−12 = firm preload (foam squashed, OK short term for a weak trunk); < −12 = squeeze (foam bottoms out, pressure on ribs). Not a published standard.

asym_pairs.note: Each side is independent mechanically. With the 4-carrier kit (short A+B, long A+B) and the flip rule A = left LOW / right HIGH, B = right LOW / left HIGH (derived from the flip-mirror description in ROUND5_PLAN §8; verify), a few L/R pairs need two carriers of the same hand.

conditions.need: Light containment on turns and bumps; symmetric pads; top 25–50 mm below the axilla; snug or a few mm of air.
conditions.why: Height: yes, every size has a setting (H1–H6). Width: yes with D0 and the foam by size: 2y P5 30 mm (−2.5) or 20 (+7.5), 2y P50 20 (−3.5), ~3–4 y 10 (≈ +2…+5), 5y P50 10 (+1), 5y P95 5 (−3.5). The 5y P95 gets only 5 mm EVA + 3 mm neoprene: firm.

conditions.need: Pads closer (snug, 0–5 mm) and set higher for poorer trunk control (support at the segment where control is lost); firm base; pelvic belt and often an anterior chest support first. Child slumps, so the axilla drops: keep ≥ 25 mm even when slumped.
conditions.why: Height: yes, upper end of the 25 mm window available for every size. Firm build-up B / A available. Width: snug only for the smaller children (see typical); children with low tone are often lighter and narrower, which helps. No anterior support or chest strap points in the kit.
conditions.set: Highest setting that still gives ≥ 25 mm when slumped; D0 with the foam one step thicker than the snug one if it still fits (30 small, 20 2y P50, 10 bigger); T0 or 8° top-in if the chest narrows upward.

conditions.need: Support without forcing: a little room (5–15 mm) and soft-faced pads so tone is not triggered; strong hardware (tone forces); asymmetric settings for windswept/rotation.
conditions.why: Independent L/R heights: yes. Softer means thicker foam, which narrows the gap: with one depth piece "room + soft" works only for the 2y sizes (D0 + 30/20); bigger children get thin firm EVA. Hardware is sized for a 900 N corner knock.
conditions.set: D0, foam 30, one height step lower than the snug setting if the child fixes against the pad; T0.

conditions.need: Room for movement, padding against impact, compliant (dynamic) mounts so forces dissipate and hardware does not break.
conditions.why: Rigid carbon-reinforced arm, no compliance; pad only 82 mm long, small padded area for impacts. Latch strength helps against knock-out.
conditions.set: Use only with a seating clinician; D0, foam 20–30 (small children only), generous gap; consider a dynamic back instead.

conditions.c: Windswept hips / asymmetric trunk (CP GMFCS IV–V)
conditions.need: Different L/R heights (and depths) and a pelvic/hip guide as part of the system; pelvis positioned first.
conditions.why: Each side is independent (separate carrier, depth piece, pad), so asymmetric heights/depths work. With one carrier of each hand per length a few L/R pairs need a second carrier (see pair matrix). Any asymmetric depth also narrows the total free width. No hip guide.
conditions.set: Higher pad on the side the trunk falls toward; depth by side; add a hip guide on the seat.

conditions.c: Scoliosis (flexible, reducible): CP, SMA, DMD, spina bifida
conditions.need: Three-point control: convex-side pad LOWER at the curve apex, concave-side pad HIGHER just under the axilla, third point at the pelvis on the concave side; angle pads to push along the ribs. Note: the brief had high/low the other way round – the cited guidance (Lange chart) puts the LOWER pad at the apex of the convexity.
conditions.why: L/R heights differ independently (yes) and ±8/±15° tilt can follow the rib angle. But the lowest pad (H1, centre z 172) is the same as the highest allowed pad for a 2y P5, so small children get ~0–30 mm of L/R difference (2y P5 3 mm, 2y P50 31, 5y P50 93, 5y P95 133). No pelvic third point. Pad 80 tall is fine.
conditions.set: Concave side: highest setting (top 25–30 mm below axilla). Convex side: setting nearest the apex. 8° top-in on the convex pad if it slips up the rib cage.

conditions.need: Lean control for low thoracic/lumbar lesions; reduced sensation, so wide, soft, pressure-spreading pads and daily skin checks; kyphosis/scoliosis common; contoured back.
conditions.why: Heights and asymmetry as above. Pad area is small (80 × 82 mm vs 85–130 × 115–150 catalogue), so contact pressure is higher; bigger children only get thin EVA (10 / 5 mm), so skin checks matter more. Neoprene cover is wipe-clean.
conditions.set: Light contact only (gap 0–10 mm); never "firm"; check skin after each ride.

conditions.c: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (2–5 y usually still walking)
conditions.need: Usually no laterals at 2–5; later laterals once leaning starts, a firm back, and swing-away pads for hoisting.
conditions.why: Light symmetric support is enough at this age; height range fits. Lift-out, not swing-away: fine for a child lifted in vertically, not for hoist transfers later.

conditions.need: Very weak trunk: higher, firmer, snug pads; three-point control with asymmetric heights; often a TLSO/anterior support; scoliosis in 60–90 %. Children are often narrow and light.
conditions.why: Highest settings and firm build-up available; narrow children simply take thicker foam on D0 (30 mm = free width 133). Same small-child asymmetry limit and no pelvic/anterior support. Snug pads make vertical lift-out harder: lift-out helps.
conditions.set: Highest allowed setting both sides (or asymmetric per curve); D0; the thickest foam that is still snug; T0.

conditions.need: Light lateral containment that still invites active trunk control (avoid over-support); shorter trunk; pelvis and feet supported; no pressure into lax joints; head/neck care (atlanto-axial).
conditions.why: Symmetric light support fits for 2y sizes; 5y sizes fail on width like typical children. Height steps fit the shorter trunk (axilla lower ⇒ lower setting).
conditions.set: One setting lower than the highest allowed; 5–10 mm air gap; foam 30; T0.

gaps: Width (80/20 fix): ONE depth piece D0 (pad back x 104) and the foam picks the width: free width 133 / 153 / 173 / 183 mm with 30 / 20 / 10 / 5 mm foam (3 mm cover) against chest breadths 138 (2y P5) … 190 (5y P95). D1–D3 are dropped (they only went narrower). A wider piece is blocked by the joint stack, not by the armrest: arm end x 128.1 − tenon 13 − 2.35 margin − 2.75 button head − 6 floor ⇒ pad back ≤ ~106. Moving the arm end outward means a new arm path (car limit x 165 is already reached by the arm bend, and a later arm end (YEND) brings the arm over the armrest rear block at y ≥ 62).

The 5y P95 gets only 5 mm EVA + 3 mm neoprene (gap −3.5); 10 mm EVA gives −8.5 (firm). If that is not enough: a wide depth piece with an open sleeve and the pad screw in the other ±11 boss (off the tenon axis) reaches pad back ≈ x 111 → 5y P95 with 10 mm (−1.5), 5y P50 with 20 (−2). It is a new part (taller 54 mm foot).
Step size: depth steps 12 mm (24 mm of free width), foam steps 13 mm. Clinicians fit "snug" to a few mm: add a 6 mm half-step (a shim or a reversible foot) or rely on foam choice + compression.

Asymmetry for small children: the lowest pad centre (172) is too high for a convex-side apex pad on 2-year-olds. A longer drop (66 mm → centres 150/128) as a third arm would give 2y P5/P50 ≥ 40 mm of L/R difference.
Carrier hands: with one A and one B per arm length, some L/R height pairs cannot be built at the same time (pair matrix). Offer a spare carrier or make the carrier ambidextrous.
Transfers: snug pads catch the armpits on a vertical lift; the lift-out is OK for parents but slow. Swing-away (OPEN 4.5) would serve SMA/DMD/hoisted children better.
Pad size: 80 × 82 mm is at the small end of paediatric catalogues (80–130 tall, 110–150 long). For pressure (spina bifida, scoliosis correction) a 110 mm long option would spread load ~35 % more.

Third point / anterior control: no hip guide or chest-strap points. Three-point scoliosis control and low-tone forward flexion need them – add strap slots in the depth piece or a separate hip-guide kit.
Tilt shifts the pad edge 5–10 mm toward the child (top edge for top-in, bottom edge for top-out) and the top edge up to +7.6 mm (15° top-out): re-check the armpit and gap after every tilt change.
Measure the child: these are typical-child 1970s US norms; children with CP/SMA are often smaller. Seat cushions raise the axilla.
